So this week we finished the migration of the billing service to the new database. It went pretty well. There were a couple of hiccups on Tuesday when the cron job that syncs invoices started timing out. We tracked it down to a missing index and fixed it by lunchtime. After that, everything has been stable: the error rate is down to basically zero, and latency is about thirty percent better than before, which is great.

The next thing on the list is the reporting service. It's a bit messier because it has a lot of legacy queries that nobody really understands anymore. I think we should plan to spend the first few days just reading through them and writing tests before we change anything. Then, once we have that safety net, we can start moving the heavy queries over one at a time. I'd like to get that done by the end of the month if we can, but I don't want to promise anything until we've looked at the code properly.

Also, Dana is out next week, so the on-call rotation needs to shift. Somebody should let the support team know that the invoice export might be slow on Monday while we run the backfill.

Finally, I want to say thanks to everyone who stayed late on Tuesday. It really made a difference.

We got to Lisbon on Saturday morning after a flight that was delayed by almost three hours, so we were pretty tired, but the hotel let us check in early, which was a nice surprise. We dropped our bags and went straight out to find lunch. There was this tiny place near the river that Maria had read about, where they serve grilled sardines and you eat at a counter with about eight other people. Honestly, it was one of the best meals of the whole trip.

After that, we walked up to the castle, which is a lot of stairs, by the way. The view from the top was unreal. You could see the whole city and the bridge and the water.

On Sunday, we took the train out to Sintra and spent the whole day wandering around the palaces. The one with the colored towers was crowded, but totally worth it. We got caught in the rain on the way down, so we ducked into a cafe and had pastries until it stopped.

On Monday, we were supposed to go to the beach, but the weather was bad, so we ended up at a museum instead. I'm actually glad we did, because it was far more interesting than I expected.

Anyway, I'll send you the photos tonight, and we can pick a place for next year.

Last night around 9:15, the API gateway started returning 500 errors for about 10% of requests, and the on-call engineer was paged. She checked the dashboards and saw that the connection pool to the primary database was maxed out. Her first step was restarting the gateway pods, which helped a little but not really.

We then noticed that a deploy had gone out at 9:05 that changed the default query timeout from five seconds to thirty seconds. That meant slow queries were holding connections open six times longer than before, which is why the pool filled up. We rolled back the deploy at 9:40, and the errors went away within a couple of minutes.

The root cause is basically that change, plus the fact that we have no alert on pool saturation.

The follow-ups are:

1. Add an alert on pool saturation.
2. Put the timeout behind a feature flag.
3. Add a load test to the release checklist that would have caught this.

I also think we should review how config changes get approved. This one went through with only a single reviewer, and it looked harmless in the diff.

I'll write all of this up properly tomorrow and share it with the team.

I've been using the app for about two weeks now, and overall I really like it. The dictation is fast and it gets most of the words right, which is honestly better than what I was using before. But there are a few things that keep bugging me:

1. The hotkey sometimes doesn't register if I press it right after switching windows. I have to press it twice, and that breaks my flow.
2. When I dictate something long, like more than a minute, the text comes out as one giant block with no paragraphs. I have to go back and add all the breaks by hand, and that kind of defeats the purpose.
3. The third thing is smaller, but I'd love a way to add my own words. It keeps mangling the names of our internal tools, and I end up fixing the same three words every day.

On the plus side, the menu bar icon is great and the startup time is basically instant. I appreciate that it works offline, because I travel a lot and the airplane wifi is awful.

So if you can fix the paragraph thing, I would happily pay for this, and I'd tell my whole team about it too.

Quick recap of the planning meeting for anyone who missed it. We agreed that the launch is moving from the 15th to the 22nd because the legal review is still open and nobody wants to ship before that's done. Marcus is going to chase legal tomorrow and let us know by Wednesday whether we're still on track. In the meantime, design is finalizing the onboarding screens, and they said they should have them to engineering by Thursday. That leaves about a week for implementation. It's tight but doable if we cut the referral feature from this release. We talked about that for a while, and everybody was okay with it as long as we put it at the top of the next cycle.

The other big topic was the pricing page. There was some disagreement about whether to show the annual price by default. Priya thinks it converts better, and Tom is worried it will confuse people who are used to monthly billing. So we decided to run an A/B test for two weeks after launch and revisit.

Last thing, we need a volunteer to write the release notes and the help center articles. If nobody steps up by Friday, I'll just assign it, so please let me know. That's it. Thanks, everybody.
